summary: Discussion segment in which the assistant explains why Tailscale's native tools (tailcat, tailscale serve, tsnsrv) all produce machine-first or service-tailnet naming, and proposes split DNS on homelab to achieve the user's desired service.machine shape (e.g. gizmo.genge, gizmo.forge). The assistant lays out dnsmasq + restricted-nameserver setup, Vite allowlist changes per machine, and TLS options (plain HTTP over WireGuard vs. mkcert private CA), suggesting a hosts-file test on the user's laptop as a quick proof-of-concept.
decisions: tsnsrv chosen over tailscale serve for multiple services: each service becomes its own tailnet node on 443 with its own name, avoiding port juggling and per-app base-path surgery.
Tailnet rename considered as the cheap path to nicer ts.net URLs, but rejected by the user because the goal is service.machine, not service.tailnet.
Split DNS via dnsmasq on homelab (100.72.105.54) with Tailscale restricted nameservers chosen as the mechanism to produce service.machine names across all tailnet devices.
TLS deferred as a separate decision: plain HTTP over WireGuard (with secure-context caveat) vs. mkcert private CA; no public CA path is available for non-ts.net names.
